notes: One entry per theme. css = the file in src/css that holds the theme's [data-palette] block; Purple has none because it is the :root base inside theme-base.css.
ground is oled | dark | light. The runtime derives <html data-theme> from it: oled -> amoled, dark -> dark, light -> light.
family groups a dark/light pair for apps that offer a dark/light switch (laserlloyd <-> laserlloyd-light).
set is core (shipped by default) or opt-in (only where an app manifest names it).

contrastProfile (optional) names the floor set tools/check_contrast.py applies: standard (the brief's table, the default) or night (red-on-black night themes, where text gains luminance only by moving toward orange: the text floors become primary 5.5, secondary 4.5, tertiary 4, disabled 2 and md-bold 6; structure, text-ladder and colour-separation checks are added, APCA is reported, and a zero-blue audit runs).

redesign (optional, core themes only) records an owner-approved redesign: the theme's values no longer come from design/output, so sync_theme.py's core drift guard skips it. Forest was redesigned on 2026-09-25.

coreFixes (optional, core themes only) lists approved token fixes, one object per round (date, tokens as token -> value, review, note). The core theme file may differ from design/output only in those tokens (and comments), and must hold exactly the recorded values; sync_theme.py's drift guard checks both. Purple's file is theme-base.css.
swatch is the picker dot colour from the specimen board. fonts are web-font families the theme names first in its stacks; every stack falls back to system fonts, so none of them has to be installed.
